ranking.title: 211.87 Retesting of approved components, drug product containers, and closures.
211.110 Sampling and testing of in-process materials and drug products.

rows.text: To assure that a drug product meets applicable standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity at the time of use, it shall bear an expiration date determined by appropriate stability testing described in § 211.166.

passages.text:
1. Purpose

To define how stability studies are planned and run, how expiry dates are assigned and printed, and how reserve samples of finished product are kept, for products made at the Chennai site.

4. Stability programme

4.1 Every product has a written stability protocol, approved by QA, and the protocol is followed for every batch placed on study. 4.2 The protocol states how many units are pulled at each time point, chosen statistically for each attribute tested, and the test intervals: 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24 and 36 months. 4.3 Samples are stored in qualified chambers at 30 C / 75% RH (long term) and 40 C / 75% RH (accelerated); chamber conditions are logged every 15 minutes. 4.4 Only validated, stability-indicating test methods are used (SOP-QC-002). 4.5 Stability samples are packed i

5. Expiry dating

5.1 The expiry date of each product is set from its long-term stability data and is printed on every label. For a new product, a tentative expiry date of 24 months may be set from six months of accelerated data. 5.2 The label states the storage condition the expiry date depends on, for example Store below 30 C, protect from moisture. 5.3 The expiry date appears on the label in the form required by 21 CFR 201.17.

rows.text: Expiration dates shall appear on labeling in accordance with the requirements of § 201.17 of this chapter.

passages.text:
1. Purpose

To define how stability studies are planned and run, how expiry dates are assigned and printed, and how reserve samples of finished product are kept, for products made at the Chennai site.

5. Expiry dating

5.1 The expiry date of each product is set from its long-term stability data and is printed on every label. For a new product, a tentative expiry date of 24 months may be set from six months of accelerated data. 5.2 The label states the storage condition the expiry date depends on, for example Store below 30 C, protect from moisture. 5.3 The expiry date appears on the label in the form required by 21 CFR 201.17.

6. Reserve samples

6.1 An identified reserve sample, representative of each batch of finished product, is kept in its market pack in the retention room at the storage condition on the label. 6.2 Each reserve sample holds at least twice the quantity needed for full release testing. 6.3 Reserve samples are kept until six months after the expiry date of the batch, then destroyed under QA witness. 6.4 Once a year each reserve sample is examined visually for evidence of deterioration, unless the examination would affect the integrity of the sample; any deterioration found is investigated under SOP
